content: Jacuzzi is a company that specializes in manufacturing whirlpool bathtubs and hot tubs. Their first product was a bathtub equipped with massaging jets. Over time, the term Jacuzzi has become a genericized trademark, often used to describe any bath with water jets, even if not made by the company. Similarly, spas and hot tubs are sometimes incorrectly referred to as Jacuzzis. The company emphasizes its unique identity with the slogan, They are Jacuzzi, and everyone else's are just hot tubs, and currently markets itself with the tagline, Jacuzzi: The Home Spa Experience. In the early 1900s, seven brothers from the Jacuzzi family emigrated from Italy to the United States, eventually settling in Berkeley, California, where they worked as machinists. One of the brothers, Rachele Jacuzzi, became inspired by an air show at the 1915 Panama-Pacific Exposition in San Francisco and began manufacturing aircraft propellers. The family business, known as Jacuzzi Bros., remained operational until 1976, though its product line evolved over the years. After a tragic plane crash in 1921 that claimed the life of their brother Giocondo, the company ceased aircraft production. Rachele redirected the company’s expertise in hydraulic aircraft pumps to develop a new type of deep well agricultural pump in 1925. In 1948, another brother, Candido Jacuzzi, innovatively applied the company’s pump technology to create a submersible bathtub pump for his son, Kenneth, who had developed severe rheumatoid arthritis at just 15 months old. Kenneth required regular hydrotherapy treatments at hospitals, but Candido sought to alleviate his son’s pain at home. He adapted the industrial water pumps to provide soothing whirlpool treatments in a bathtub. This invention, known as the J-300 pump, was marketed in 1955. Kenneth later went on to lead the company. During this time, the company hired Jack Benny as a spokesperson and began promoting the whirlpool bath as a therapeutic aid, selling it in drugstores and bath supply shops. To increase public awareness, portable Jacuzzis were featured as prizes on the television show Queen for a Day. Initially marketed as a relief for overworked housewives, the product gained significant attention when Hollywood stars like Randolph Scott and Jayne Mansfield endorsed it, elevating its status to a symbol of luxury. In 1968, Candido Jacuzzi introduced the first self-contained, fully integrated whirlpool bath by incorporating jets directly into the sides of the tub. This innovation, patented under 3297025, marked the birth of a new industry and era of whirlpool bathing. The Jacuzzi became synonymous with a luxurious lifestyle, and portable units were installed in homes, recreation centers, and hotels worldwide. By the 1970s, the company expanded its product line to include larger units with built-in heating and filtration systems, laying the foundation for the modern spa industry. These models could be used as hot tubs, whirlpool baths, or both, and were suitable for indoor or outdoor installation. The medical community quickly recognized the therapeutic benefits of Jacuzzi products, incorporating them into hydrotherapy programs. Physical therapists and orthopedic specialists prescribed their use in clinics and homes. Hollywood celebrities further popularized the brand by adopting it for personal use. Today, Jacuzzi-branded hot tubs, baths, showers, sinks, toilets, and accessories are widely found in residential homes, hotels, and cruise ships, as well as in high-end spas globally. The company distributes its products in approximately 60 countries. The Jacuzzi family’s story exemplifies the classic narrative of European immigrants achieving the American Dream. After arriving from Italy in the early 1900s, they initially worked in agriculture and small aircraft manufacturing before revolutionizing the pump industry in 1925 with an efficient new design that earned them a Gold Medal at the California State Fair in 1930. In 1968, Roy Jacuzzi introduced the Roman Bathtub, the first integrated whirlpool bath featuring patented jets that delivered a 50/50 air-to-water ratio, creating a unique and unparalleled bathing experience. This signature jet technology remains a hallmark of Jacuzzi products today. Early advertising campaigns featured Suzanne Somers, then a model, to promote the brand. By the 1970s, the company began producing larger spa units with advanced features, ushering in the modern spa industry. These innovations allowed families and friends to enjoy a vacation-like experience in their own backyards. In the 1980s, Jacuzzi expanded its product line to include multi-use models that functioned as both hot tubs and whirlpool baths. The company’s assembly plant in Chino, California, became the first ISO 9001-certified hot tub production facility in the world, capable of producing up to 300 spas per day for domestic and international markets. Today, Jacuzzi is the most recognized name globally in jetted baths, spas, and hot tubs, symbolizing luxury, relaxation, and innovation.
